title: Get a residential building permit (including trade permits) and schedule inspections
question: I want to build, add on, renovate, or do electrical, plumbing or mechanical work on my home in Staunton. Do I need a permit, how do I apply, and how are inspections scheduled?
office: Community Development Department, Building Services Division (the City of Staunton's local building department, headed by the Building Official)
summary: Staunton's Building Services Division (Community Development) enforces Virginia's Uniform Statewide Building Code. New homes, additions, decks, garages, pools, demolition and most structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and gas work need a permit before work starts; small sheds, most fences and ordinary repairs usually do not. Since May 5, 2026, apply in the city's online portal (paper is still accepted at City Hall) with a site sketch or plat and plans. Trade work needs separate permits. Real estate taxes must be paid first, and historic (Certificate of Appropriateness), water and sewer connection, erosion control and driveway approvals may apply. The city estimates ten business days for residential review; building permit fees are set in City Code § 15.10.120, whose amounts were not read. Post the permit, request inspections in the portal, and appeal code decisions to the local Board of Building Code Appeals within 30 calendar days.

steps.step: Check whether the work needs a building permit
steps.who: Property owner, or the contractor or designer working for them
steps.how: Under the Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code (USBC), a permit is needed before building or demolishing a structure; adding or removing walls or partitions; work on structural parts, required fire- or smoke-rated assemblies or exits; installing or altering water supply, drainage or vent piping, electric wiring, fire protection, mechanical or fuel systems or other regulated equipment; removing or disturbing asbestos-containing materials during construction or demolition; a change of occupancy that needs a new certificate of occupancy under the Virginia Existing Building Code; or moving a lot line in a way that makes an existing building less safe. Exempt work includes one-story detached sheds and playhouses up to 256 square feet, most fences (not pool barriers or fences required for pedestrian safety), concrete or masonry walls up to six feet, retaining walls holding back less than three feet of fill, pools of 150 square feet or less that are under 24 inches deep, and ordinary repairs such as replacing windows and doors of similar operation and opening size, plumbing fixtures, switches, receptacles and light fixtures, mechanical appliances not fueled by gas or oil, roof covering or siding (unless the nominal design wind speed is over 100 mph; see caveats), flooring, cabinets, trim, paint and wallpaper. Exempt work must still meet the code, an owner or owner's agent can ask for a permit (and then inspections apply), and the building official may require permits for replacement siding, roofing and windows in a historic district and for any exempt item in a special flood hazard area. The city asks people to contact Building Services about exemptions.
steps.deadline: Before work starts; for emergency construction, alterations or equipment replacement, the application is due by the end of the first working day after the work begins. The building official may also authorize work to start before the application is received or the permit is issued.
steps.quote: Please contact the Building Services Division about what projects may be exempt from permits

steps.step: Identify every permit the project needs
steps.who: Property owner or contractor
steps.how: Staunton issues a building permit for single-family and two-family dwellings, accessory buildings and garages, additions, alterations, decks and porches, swimming pools, change of use, demolition, generators, solar installations (a ground-mounted solar array also needs its own building permit for the ground structure) and residential elevators. Electrical, plumbing, mechanical and gas work each need a separate trade permit. Projects with more than two units are handled as commercial projects.
steps.quote: Separate permits are required for electrical, plumbing, mechanical, and gas.

steps.step: If the property is in a historic district, get a Certificate of Appropriateness first
steps.who: Property owner or agent; Community Development, Planning & Zoning Division (staff review) and the Historic Preservation Commission
steps.how: Check whether the property is in one of Staunton's historic districts. If it is, a Certificate of Appropriateness may be required before the building permit is issued; the Building Services page says one is required for plumbing, mechanical and gas permits and solar installations in a historic district ('may be required' for building, electrical and generator permits), and a site sketch is then needed for trade permits. The city's Certificate of Appropriateness application has two routes. Administrative review by staff (about ten business days) covers signs, screening of mechanical equipment, removing vinyl or metal siding to expose the original siding, replacing gutters with metal half-round gutters, and in-kind roof replacement of more than half of a roof element. Other work goes to the Historic Preservation Commission, which meets on the fourth Tuesday of the month at 5:30 p.m.; the agenda deadline is the first Tuesday, and the applicant must attend. Submit sketches or elevations, a site plan or plat, photographs and a materials list (digital plans to permits@fileshare.ci.staunton.va.us); historic review permits can also be applied for in the online portal. A Commission approval expires 12 months after it is granted.
steps.deadline: Before the building or trade permit is issued; for Commission review, apply by the first Tuesday of the month for that month's meeting
steps.quote: If the property is located in a historic district, a Certificate of Appropriateness may be required before issuance of a Building Permit.

steps.step: For a new water or sewer connection, apply to the City Engineer's Office
steps.who: Property owner; Public Works, Engineering Division
steps.how: Submit the Application for Water and Sewer Connection and Facility Fees to the City Engineer's Office so the city can confirm that service is available and set the fees. The fees depend on the water meter size; if rock or other unusual conditions raise the installation cost, the applicant agrees on the form to pay the direct cost plus 30%.
steps.deadline: Before any building permit is issued
steps.fee: Water and sewer connection and facility fees: for a typical single-family home (5/8-inch meter, 4-inch sewer lateral) the city's July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 schedule shows $5,600 for water and $9,950 for sewer, $15,550 in all (see fees and caveats)
steps.quote: This must be completed prior to issuance of any building permits.

steps.step: For a new house or other land disturbance, complete the erosion and sediment control requirements
steps.who: Property owner; Community Development, Environmental Programs Division
steps.how: For a single-family home or a site under 10,000 square feet, the owner signs an Agreement in Lieu of a Plan, pays the fee and posts a surety, attends a pre-construction meeting on erosion and sediment (E&S) controls, and has a city E&S/VSMP inspector visit the site and approve the initial controls. The city's agreement form names the landowner and a responsible land disturber, estimates the dwelling footprint, decks, porches and driveway area, and grants the city right of entry for inspections. The agreement must be kept on the work site, the city must be told when work starts and when it is finished, and grading, excavating and construction may not start until the city has approved the erosion controls. The form asks whether the lot is part of a larger plan of development over one acre platted after June 30, 2004; if so, VSMP permit coverage and a stormwater pollution prevention plan (SWPPP; the city has a Single Family SWPPP form) are also needed. Larger sites need an approved E&S and stormwater plan and a city Land Disturbing Permit.
steps.fee: Agreement in Lieu of a Plan: $250 fee and a $2,500 surety
steps.quote: An Agreement in Lieu of a Plan must be completed and signed by the property owner and include payment of fee and submission of surety.

steps.step: For a new or changed driveway across the sidewalk, curb or street edge, get a Driveway Entrance Permit
steps.who: Property owner; Public Works, Engineering Division
steps.how: Apply online or on paper with a site sketch or plat showing the driveway location. The owner pays for the work, which must follow city specifications under Engineering Division supervision. The Engineering Division estimates ten business days. The paper application (made under City Code Title 12.20) asks whether new construction needing a building permit is involved and whether the site is in a historic district, and says the authorization becomes void unless construction begins within six months of the application.
steps.deadline: Start construction within six months of the application date, or the authorization becomes void
steps.quote: This approval is authorized from the office of the City Engineer only upon application by the property owner.

steps.step: Make sure the real estate taxes on the property are paid
steps.who: Property owner; City Treasurer's Office
steps.how: The city will not issue a building permit until all real estate taxes on the property are paid. State law lets a locality require an owner-applicant (including the owner's agent) to pay obligations that are a lien on the property, but a tenant or easement holder who applies cannot be refused a permit only because the owner owes the city.
steps.quote: All real estate property taxes must be paid prior to issuance of a building permit.

steps.step: Decide who applies: the owner as their own builder, a licensed contractor, or an agent
steps.who: Property owner, licensed contractor, or an agent authorized by the owner
steps.how: A contractor gives a Virginia contractor license number and expiration date (and the email used on the portal). An owner doing the work on their own home signs the owner statement on the application that they are not subject to contractor licensing and that any workers they hire are properly licensed; Virginia exempts an owner building or improving one primary residence for their own use in any 24-month period, but the work must still meet the building code. An agent signs that the work has the owner's consent; the trade permit application asks for the owner's written authorization. The permit cannot be issued without a license number or the written exemption statement, and state law also requires the applicant to show that the local taxes or license fees needed to contract for the work have been paid.
steps.quote: I am not subject to licensure as a contractor or subcontractor

steps.step: Prepare the site sketch or plat, building plans and other documents
steps.who: Property owner, contractor or designer
steps.how: Required for a house: a site sketch or plat (property lines, streets and alleys, setback lines, existing and proposed structures including decks, porches, stoops, chimneys, mechanical equipment, stairs, walks and retaining walls, driveways and parking, sizes and distances to property lines) and building plans no larger than 24 by 36 inches (complete scope of work and any phases, floor plans with room labels and dimensions, existing and proposed plans for alterations and additions, a detailed wall section, front and side elevations, and a foundation or footing plan). Optional: a RESCheck energy report, and Health Department construction permits if a well or septic system serves the property. Additions, alterations, decks and porches also list the Asbestos Regulations Compliance Form; demolition needs utility disconnection notices and the asbestos form. City templates include a wall section form, a deck construction form and a site plan example. The city's Current Building Codes and Design Criteria sheet lists the code editions in force (2021 Virginia codes) and local design values, such as a 43 psf ground snow load and a 24-inch frost line depth.
steps.quote: Required Documents: Site Sketch/Plat, Building Plans.

steps.step: Complete the Asbestos Regulations Compliance Form for renovation work
steps.who: Property owner or the owner's legal agent
steps.how: The city's form applies to all renovation permits, including trade permits. The owner of an existing home with four or fewer dwelling units answers whether the work is renovation or demolition for commercial development; if it is not, they sign the form. State law requires the asbestos inspection certification only for buildings first permitted before January 1, 1985, and does not apply to single-family homes or housing with four or fewer units unless they are renovated or demolished for commercial or public development, or where the asbestos-containing material involved is below set amounts. Others may need an inspection by a Virginia licensed asbestos inspector (re-roofing, re-flooring or re-siding may instead be treated as presumed asbestos handled by a licensed contractor). If asbestos is abated, a licensed contractor applies for the abatement permit, and the Asbestos Re-Occupancy Certification is filed (uploaded in the portal) before the area is reoccupied.
steps.quote: It must be completed for all renovation permit applications, including electrical, fire protection, mechanical, plumbing and sign permits.

steps.step: Apply for the building permit online (or on paper at City Hall)
steps.who: Applicant (owner, contractor or agent); Community Development, Building Services Division
steps.how: Since May 5, 2026 new applications go through the city's online permitting portal: create an account (an existing city Business License or Personal Property Tax account also works), enter the project details and upload the plans as PDF files. Paper applications are still accepted at the Community Development office (City Hall, 3rd floor): one paper copy of the plans, or email a digital set to permits@fileshare.ci.staunton.va.us with the project address in the subject line. For a one- or two-family dwelling the application can name a mechanics' lien agent; if none is named, the permit says "None Designated." State rules say no applicant can be required to appear in person.
steps.fee: Building permit fee under the fee schedule in Staunton City Code § 15.10.120 (amounts not read)
steps.quote: All applicants are encouraged to process their request through the online citizen permitting portal.

steps.step: Apply for each trade permit (electrical, plumbing, mechanical, gas)
steps.who: Licensed tradesperson or contractor, or the owner doing their own work; Building Services Division
steps.how: Apply online or with the Trade Permit Application. A site sketch is needed only in a historic district; plumbing work that needs an easement needs a copy of it. When a fuel-burning appliance is replaced or newly installed and vents into an existing chimney, the installer certifies on the city's Existing Chimney Certification that the chimney or vent is properly sized, clean and in working order, unless the city inspects it. Heating and cooling equipment must be sized under the code sections listed on the form. Trade permits are not revoked for inactivity while the building permit is still in effect.
steps.fee: Trade permit fee under Staunton City Code § 15.10.120 (amounts not read)
steps.quote: Estimated Processing Time: One (1) business day unless historic approval is required.

steps.step: Plan review; answer any request for more information
steps.who: Building Services Division (and zoning review against Title 18 setbacks); applicant
steps.how: Plans are reviewed electronically. If more information is needed, the applicant is emailed and resubmits in the portal (the city publishes how-to guides for resubmitting). A permit is issued only when the plans show the work will meet building and zoning rules. To use an alternative to a code provision, ask the building official in writing for a modification (the city's Application for Modification); the decision is made in writing. If the application is denied, Building Services must explain the reasons in writing, and the applicant may revise and resubmit. An application is treated as abandoned six months after filing unless it has been pursued in good faith or a permit issued; the building official may extend that time for justifiable cause.
steps.deadline: City estimate: ten business days for residential building permits; state rule: review within a reasonable time and issue as soon as practicable
steps.quote: Estimated Processing Time: Ten (10) business days.

steps.step: Pay the fees and receive the permit by email
steps.who: Applicant; Building Services Division
steps.how: The permit is not issued until the fees are paid (the building official may allow delayed payment). Once approved, the permit is emailed to the applicant and lists the minimum inspections required.
steps.fee: Permit fee under Staunton City Code § 15.10.120; the state requires a 2% Building Code Academy levy on permit fees
steps.quote: Once the permit has been approved, the applicant will receive the permit by email.

steps.step: Post the permit at the job site and keep the approved plans there
steps.who: Permit holder (owner or contractor)
steps.how: For a one- or two-family dwelling the permit must be posted on the property, visible, before any labor or materials go into the job, and stay posted until the work is complete. One set of approved construction documents must be kept at the building site for the inspector, and an erosion control Agreement in Lieu of a Plan must also be kept on site.
steps.deadline: Before any labor is performed or material furnished
steps.quote: The permit shall be posted on the property before any labor is performed or any material furnished on the property for which the building permit is issued.

steps.step: Request each required inspection
steps.who: Permit holder; Building Services Division inspectors
steps.how: When the work reaches a stage that needs an inspection, request it in the online portal. The city's Required Inspections sheet lists footings (including pier footings) before concrete, foundation before framing or backfill, framing (structural members and fasteners) before the slab pour, insulation, siding or brick veneer go in, slab preparation before concrete, electrical, mechanical and plumbing rough-in before concealment, insulation (energy conservation materials) before concealment, and final; the minimum inspections for each job are listed on the permit. For permits issued before May 5, 2026, call the Community Development office (540.332.3862) to request inspections. In a flood hazard area, submit the lowest-floor elevation certificate once the lowest floor is placed and before building further. The permit holder provides any ladder, scaffolding or test equipment needed.
steps.deadline: When each stage is ready and before the work is covered
steps.quote: At that time, inspections can be requested through the online portal.

steps.step: Pass each inspection, or correct the defects and ask for a reinspection
steps.who: Building Services Division inspector; permit holder
steps.how: The inspector approves the work in writing or gives written notice of defective work (on request, citing the code section). Defects must be corrected and reinspected before they are covered. If the city cannot inspect within two working days of the request, the building official must accept a report from a third-party inspector approved under the official's written policy.
steps.deadline: Rejected third-party reports must be explained in writing within two working days
steps.quote: The building official shall either approve the work in writing or give written notice of defective work to the permit holder.

steps.step: For a new house, deliver the duct leakage and energy test reports to Building Services
steps.who: Mechanical contractor or tester; permit holder
steps.how: Unless exempt under VRC § N1103.3.5, a test report for each ducted HVAC system in a newly built dwelling must be mailed or hand delivered to Building Services Division, City Hall, Third Floor, 116 W. Beverley St., P.O. Box 58, Staunton, VA 24402 before the certificate of occupancy; reports must not be left on the job site or handed to inspectors in the field. The city's forms list also has a Duct Leakage Testing Affidavit and a Building Envelope Leakage (blower door) Affidavit for new construction, each certified by the testing technician with a DPOR license number; the blower door affidavit shows a maximum of 5 air changes per hour at 50 Pascal. The forms read do not say how or when the two affidavits are delivered.
steps.deadline: Before the certificate of occupancy is issued
steps.quote: Reports required for code compliance shall not be left posted on job sites or hand delivered to inspectors in the field.

steps.step: Keep the permit active, or ask in writing for an extension
steps.who: Permit holder; building official
steps.how: The city's application says the permit is void if construction has not started within six months of issue. Under the USBC the building official may revoke a permit if work does not start within six months or stops for six months, and the permit holder must show progress, usually by at least one approved inspection in six months. Trade permits are not revoked while the building permit is in effect. The building official may grant written requests for extensions of up to one year each; ask in writing before the six months pass. The building official may also set a three-year limit to finish a new house, an addition or an accessory structure.
steps.deadline: Start within six months of issuance; no six-month gap in work
steps.quote: Permit void if construction not started within six (6) months of permit issuance.

steps.step: Pass the final inspection and get the certificate of occupancy
steps.who: Permit holder; Building Services Division
steps.how: After the final inspection is approved, the building official issues the certificate of occupancy for a new dwelling. An addition to a house that already has one does not need a new certificate, and an accessory structure does not need one. On request, the building official may issue a temporary certificate of occupancy before all the work is finished if that part of the building can be occupied safely.
steps.deadline: Within five working days after the final inspection is approved
steps.quote: The building official shall issue the certificate of occupancy within five working days after approval of the final inspection and when the building or structure or portion thereof is determined to be in compliance with this code and any pertinent laws or ordinances, or when otherwise entitled.

steps.step: If the project is cancelled, ask in writing for a refund
steps.who: Permit holder; Building Services Division
steps.how: Send a written request to Building Services. State rules require a refund when a permit is revoked or a project is abandoned or cancelled, up to the amount for work not done. The city's own refund rules were not found.
steps.fee: Refund up to the amount that correlates to work not completed
steps.quote: When requested in writing by a permit holder, the locality shall provide a fee refund in the case of the revocation of a permit or the abandonment or cancellation of a building project.

escalation.trigger: The city cannot make a requested inspection within two working days of the request or an agreed date
escalation.next: A report from a third-party inspector approved under the building official's written policy; the building official must approve the report unless there is cause to reject it
escalation.deadline: A rejected report must be explained in writing within two working days of receipt
escalation.quote: Failure to approve a report shall be in writing within two working days of receiving it stating the reason for the rejection.

escalation.trigger: Permit denied (Building Services must give written reasons), or any other decision applying the building code: refused modification, notice of defective work, permit revocation, refused certificate of occupancy
escalation.next: Staunton Board of Building Code Appeals (the city's local board of Building Code appeals); a written request for appeal with a copy of the building official's decision
escalation.deadline: Within 30 calendar days of receiving the decision; the board meets within 30 calendar days (45 if it has regular monthly meetings) unless all parties agree to more time, with at least 14 calendar days' notice of the hearing unless the parties agree to less
escalation.quote: The applicant shall submit a written request for appeal to the LBBCA within 30 calendar days of the receipt of the decision being appealed.

escalation.trigger: Disagree with the local board's decision
escalation.next: State Building Code Technical Review Board (DHCD), using its Application for Administrative Appeal with copies of the building official's decision and the local board's decision
escalation.deadline: Within 21 calendar days of receiving the local board's decision
escalation.quote: The application for appeal shall be made to the State Review Board within 21 calendar days of the receipt of the decision to be appealed.

escalation.trigger: Disagree with the State Review Board's decision
escalation.next: Circuit court under the Administrative Process Act (notice of appeal filed with the Secretary of the Review Board)
escalation.deadline: 30 days from service of the decision (Rule 2A:2), plus 3 days if served by mail
escalation.quote: you have thirty (30) days from the date of service (the date you actually received this decision or the date it was mailed to you, whichever occurred first) within which to appeal this decision by filing a Notice of Appeal with the Secretary of the Review Board

escalation.trigger: Zoning review refused (for example a setback or use decision by the zoning administrator)
escalation.next: Staunton Board of Zoning Appeals (notice of appeal filed with the zoning administrator and the board; the city's Appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals form)
escalation.quote: The appeal shall be taken within 30 days after the decision appealed from by filing with the zoning administrator, and with the board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof.

escalation.trigger: Certificate of Appropriateness refused by the Historic Preservation Commission
escalation.next: Staunton City Council on appeal (state law lets the ordinance provide this appeal; Staunton's ordinance was not read), then the circuit court
escalation.deadline: Appeal to City Council: as the city ordinance sets (not read); circuit court petition within 30 days after City Council's final decision
escalation.quote: provided that the petition is filed within 30 days after the final decision is rendered by the governing body

escalation.trigger: A question about what the building code means, with no appeal pending
escalation.next: Informal staff opinion from DHCD's State Building Codes Office; a formal interpretation by the State Review Board must be requested by code enforcement staff with the building official's approval
escalation.basis: DHCD State Building Code Technical Review Board page (https://www.dhcd.virginia.gov/state-building-code-technical-review-board-sbctrb); Va. Code § 36-118
escalation.quote: Interpretation requests may be submitted by any code enforcement personnel with approval from the corresponding building, maintenance or fire official.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The city's Web Disclaimer & Privacy Policy bars attempts to get around the site's security features and sets no rule against quoting. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

Permit fee amounts were not found. The city's pages give no amounts and link the fee schedule (City Code § 15.10.120) to the old Code Publishing site, which refuses automated readers. The code is now on General Code's eCode360 (https://ecode360.com/ST4660), whose terms limit content to personal use and bar reproducing it for public purposes, so the section has not been checked. Ask Building Services (540.332.3862, permits@ci.staunton.va.us) for an estimate, or read § 15.10.120 yourself. Also not found: whether the state 2% levy is shown as a line or kept by the city, re-inspection or after-hours fees, the city's refund rules, and any fee for an appeal to the Board of Building Code Appeals.

Paper Building Permit Application: the 2026-07-17 Building Services page links version 639168510357930000 of the form; the quotes here come from the earlier version 639135725203530000 (Internet Archive copy of 2026-05-10). That covers the quotes in steps 8 and 19, and the current version may differ.

Documents not confirmed (the Internet Archive has no copy, and the city site refuses automated readers): the Sign Up, Log In, Apply, Schedule an Inspection and Resubmit how-to guides, the current version of the Building Permit Application (639168510357930000), the Planning & Zoning fees page, and the City Code sections the pages link (§ 15.10.120 fee schedule, Title 18 historic district and floodplain rules). The older Building Permit Brochure (2017) asks for two copies of plans; the current pages ask for one, so the brochure is not used.

Inspection scheduling: the pages read say only that inspections for permits issued from May 5, 2026 are requested in the online portal, that permits issued earlier need a call to the office, and that the minimum inspections are listed on each permit. The city's Required Inspections sheet (read) lists the seven inspections in step s16; it carries an older 'Department of Planning & Inspections' letterhead. No cut-off time, same-day or next-day rule, inspection hours or inspector call-ahead practice was found.

Board of Building Code Appeals: Staunton's board page is on stauntonva.granicus.com, which refuses automated readers, so it is not described here. No Staunton appeal form, fee, filing office or meeting schedule was found. The state rule is a written request to the board within 30 calendar days with a copy of the decision; in practice, file it through Building Services and ask for a dated receipt (USBC § 119.5 says the board marks the date received).

No answer: no deemed approval applies to building permits. The ten business days is the city's estimate; state rules require review within a reasonable time and issuance as soon as practicable, and a denial must be explained in writing. Whether delay alone can be appealed to the Board of Building Code Appeals was not established; asking for a written decision gives something to appeal.

Six-month wording: the city's application says a permit is 'void' if construction has not started within six months; USBC § 110.6 says the building official 'shall be permitted to revoke' it and allows written extensions of up to one year each. Ask for an extension in writing before six months pass.

Asbestos: the city's pages list the Asbestos Regulations Compliance Form for additions, alterations, decks, porches and demolition, and the form says it applies to all renovation permits including trade permits. State law exempts single-family homes and buildings with four or fewer units unless renovated or demolished for commercial or public development, and the form lets such owners answer two questions and sign.

The When do I need a permit? page summarises an older text of USBC § 108.1 (it mentions lead-containing materials and a change of use needing greater structural strength or fire protection). The current § 108.1 refers to asbestos-containing materials and to a change of occupancy that needs a new certificate of occupancy under the Virginia Existing Building Code. The current regulation is quoted here.

Real estate taxes: the city requires all real estate taxes to be paid before a permit is issued. Va. Code § 36-105(D)(1) lets a locality require an owner-applicant to pay obligations that are a lien on the property, but says a tenant or easement holder who applies cannot be refused only because the owner owes the city; the city pages do not mention that exception. The index marks Va. Code § 15.2-2286 'effective until January 1, 2027' with no successor text; recheck after that date.

Historic districts: the Building Services page says a Certificate of Appropriateness 'may be required' for building permits, and 'is required' for plumbing, mechanical and gas permits and solar installations in a historic district. The city's Certificate of Appropriateness form (read) describes administrative and Historic Preservation Commission review. Which districts apply, any application fee, how staff decisions are appealed and the deadline to appeal to City Council (set by local ordinance) were not read. USBC § 108.2 lets the building official require permits for replacement siding, roofing and windows in a historic district; whether Staunton does so was not found.

Floodplain: the Building Services page links Staunton's Floodplain Ordinance (City Code § 18.170) and a floodplain map; neither was read. In a special flood hazard area the building official may require permits for work that is otherwise exempt, and lowest-floor elevation documentation is required during construction.

Zoning: the pages read say permits are issued only when the work meets zoning rules and point to Title 18 setbacks, but do not say whether a separate zoning permit is needed for a house, addition or shed. The Apply Online page lists Zoning Permits under the Planning & Zoning Division. Sheds, fences and other work exempt from the building permit may still need zoning approval; ask Planning & Zoning.

Phone numbers: the When do I need a permit? page and the paper application give 540.332.3862 for the City Engineer's Office (utilities connections), while the Building Services and Engineering Division pages give 540.332.3858. The Engineering Division's own page is followed here.

Trade work by others: the owner statement on the application makes the owner responsible for making sure hired workers are properly licensed. The rules on which electrical, plumbing, gas and HVAC work needs a licensed tradesman are not covered here. The DPOR phone number comes from the city's Consumer Guide (a 2017 document, archived 2026-05-11); check it before use.
The online portal (Tyler EnerGov) was not opened; no account was created and nothing was submitted. Portal steps come from the city's pages, and the how-to PDFs were not read.

Privacy: the city's pages name the Building Official, Deputy Building Official, permit technicians, City Engineer, Engineering staff and the property maintenance inspector, and list their personal mailboxes (the Engineering page sends driveway permit questions to a staff mailbox). None of these is recorded. Only office lines, the role mailboxes permits@ci.staunton.va.us and permits@fileshare.ci.staunton.va.us (both published on the Building Services page), DHCD's sbco@ office mailbox, portals and pages are listed.

Staunton is an independent city surrounded by Augusta County. A property with a Staunton mailing address may lie in Augusta County, whose building department issues its permits. Check that the property is inside city limits.

State law quotes are matched to Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia; regulation quotes to law.lis.virginia.gov, and DHCD text to its Review Board page. The USBC adopts the International Code Council model codes by reference; those texts are not quoted.

Water and sewer fees: the amounts come from the fee table on the city's Water and Sewer Connection and Facility Fees application, which covers July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026. The city's forms page still linked that version on 2026-07-17, but the fees for the current fiscal year may differ; confirm with the Engineering Division (540.332.3858). The PDF's text layer separates the table columns, so the amounts were read from the table layout.

Roofing and siding: the city's Current Building Codes and Design Criteria sheet gives an ultimate design wind speed (VULT) of 115 mph for Risk Category II. The USBC exemption for replacing roof covering or siding on a one- or two-family home depends on the nominal design wind speed not exceeding 100 mph, which the sheet does not state. Ask Building Services before re-roofing or re-siding without a permit.

Generators: the current Building Services page lists a permit with a site sketch and building plans for a generator; the older city handout (about 2018) lists electrical and mechanical permit applications, manufacturer specifications, a three-day review and gas and electrical inspections. The current page is followed.

corrections: Method: all 104 original quotes were confirmed. The 34 Code of Virginia quotes are whitespace-normalised substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (lexflow-app-1), and the subsection labels match where the words sit; lexflow's checker (municipal.places.check_quotes) matched 34 of 34 code quotes before and after the edits. The 45 Administrative Code quotes (including the four fee and escalation quotes that cite both a statute and 13VAC5-63) were matched against the eight 13VAC5-63 pages on law.lis.virginia.gov, fetched again on 2026-10-11 (no robots.txt; 2-second spacing). The 25 City quotes were matched character for character against Internet Archive copies of the cited pages and PDFs, fetched again with the research User-Agent at 2- to 3-second spacing; www.ci.staunton.va.us still answers HTTP 403, robots.txt included (one request), and was not worked around. Twenty quotes were added or substituted and checked the same way (1 state, 9 regulation, 9 City documents, 1 DHCD page), giving 124 checked, 124 confirmed and 122 in the file. Two confirmed quotes were replaced by better-fitting ones (the water and sewer fee entry; escalation rung 7), and are not counted as removed.

Documents the draft listed as not read or not archived were found in the Internet Archive and read: the Applications, Forms, & Brochures page (2026-07-17), Required Inspections (2026-05-13), the Residential Ducted HVAC System Affidavit and Blower Door Form, the Application for Modification, the current Agreement in Lieu of a Plan, the Water and Sewer Connection application, the Driveway/Entrance Permit application, the current Existing Chimney Certification and Current Building Codes and Design Criteria. The Certificate of Appropriateness application, the Board of Zoning Appeals appeal form, the Single Family SWPPP form, the DCA6 deck guide and the generator handout were also read. Form titles f6, f8, f9, f13, f20, f21, f22 and f24 now give the documents' own titles; f20 now links the current version (1392/639141771570530000) listed on the forms page; forms f26 to f31 were added; caveats and 15 sources were updated to match.

Fees and s4: the draft said the water and sewer connection and facility fees were not stated. The application's fee table (July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026) gives $5,600 water and $9,950 sewer, $15,550 in all, for a typical single-family home with a 5/8-inch meter; the fee entry now gives the amounts and cites the PDF, with a caveat that the schedule's period has ended.

s1: 'fences' was too broad; USBC § 108.2 item 5 exempts fences except pool barriers and fences required for pedestrian safety (now 'most fences', with a legal_basis quote). Roof covering and siding replacement is exempt only where the nominal design wind speed is not over 100 mph (item 14.5, now quoted, with a caveat on Staunton's design wind speed). 'Changing the occupancy' is now limited to a change that needs a new certificate of occupancy under the VEBC, as § 108.1 says. Added the other exempt items and the § 108.1 rule that the building official may let work start before the application or permit (quoted).

s3 and escalation rung 6: the draft did not say how a Certificate of Appropriateness is obtained and called the deciding body 'the city's historic district review board'. The city's application (read) gives administrative staff review (ten business days) for listed minor work and Historic Preservation Commission review otherwise (fourth Tuesday, agenda deadline the first Tuesday, applicant must attend), and says a Commission approval expires after 12 months. s3 now says so with three local legal_basis quotes and form f26. The rung now names the Commission and says the appeal to City Council exists if the ordinance provides it (Va. Code § 15.2-2306(A)(1) lets it), since the ordinance was not read.

s5: added the Agreement in Lieu of a Plan's own terms (keep it on site, notify the city at start and completion, no work until controls are approved, responsible land disturber, the VSMP question for lots in a larger plan of development), with two local quotes, and the Single Family SWPPP form (f28).
s6: added the driveway application's rule that the authorization becomes void unless construction begins within six months of the application (local quote) and set the step's deadline.
s7: 'property owner' in Va. Code § 36-105(D)(1) includes the owner's agent; now said. s8: added the § 54.1-1111(A) requirement to show local taxes or license fees are paid (already in legal_basis).

s10: the draft did not say that the state asbestos certification applies only to buildings first permitted before January 1, 1985 (Va. Code § 36-99.7(A), now quoted), and gave the exemption as 'commercial development' only; the statute says 'commercial or public development purposes' and also excludes small amounts. Reworded.
s11: the mechanics' lien agent designation applies to one- or two-family dwellings (§ 36-98.01); now said.

s12: the Existing Chimney Certification applies to any replacement or new fuel-burning appliance using an existing chimney or vent, unless the city inspects it (USBC § 113.3.1, now quoted), not only gas appliances. Added that trade permits are not revoked for inactivity while the building permit is in effect (USBC § 110.6, now quoted).

s13: an application is abandoned after six months only if not pursued in good faith, and the building official may extend the time for justifiable cause (USBC § 108.8, now quoted). Added the modification route (USBC § 106.3, form f24), which was in legal_basis and forms but in no step.
s15: the requirement to keep approved plans on site had no basis in the file; USBC § 109.5 is now quoted.

s16: the inspection list now follows the city's Required Inspections sheet (local quote), and the lowest-floor elevation certificate in flood hazard areas is added (USBC § 113.3.2, now quoted). s18: the two affidavits are now described from the forms; the deadline is supported by a new quote from the Ducted HVAC System Test Report. s19: added the trade permit rule and that progress is usually shown by an approved inspection. s20: added the temporary certificate of occupancy (USBC § 116.1.1, now quoted).
